Lessons.Title: Let’s Make a Box
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Generalize from specific calculations to create a polynomial to model the volume of a constructed box. Interpret features of a graph of a polynomial.

Removing an equal square of side x from each corner of an L by W sheet and folding gives a box with height x and base dimensions L-2x and W-2x; V(x)=x(L-2x)(W-2x) with 0<x<min(L,W)/2. A graph must be interpreted only over the physically permitted domain.

Source activity 1.1: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Boxes: Which one doesn’t belong? Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 1.2: Building Boxes: Your teacher will give you some supplies. Construct an open-top box from a sheet of paper by cutting out a square from each corner and then folding up the sides. Calculate the volume of your box, and complete the table with your information. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial box volume
KeyConcepts.Definition: Removing an equal square of side x from each corner of an L by W sheet and folding gives a box with height x and base dimensions L-2x and W-2x; V(x)=x(L-2x)(W-2x) with 0<x<min(L,W)/2. A graph must be interpreted only over the physically permitted domain.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Apply the exact task conditions, mathematical operation, and permitted domain.
KeyConcepts.Example: For a 20 by 12 inch sheet, write the volume polynomial and evaluate at x=2. Answer: V(x)=4x^3-64x^2+240x cubic inches; V(2)=256.
